provenance.abstraction_rationale: Selected API is torch.compile. The report attributes an out-of-bounds read to torch.compile when it compiles a CPU model using indirect indexing x[self.idx] inside torch.sum. torch.sum is only mentioned, so this pattern remains scoped to torch.compile.
unresolved_information: No explicit root-cause claim was mapped in reported_diagnosis; the mechanism is based on comment-thread diagnostic text rather than a normalized root_cause_claim.
No explicit expected-behavior claim or historical oracle was mapped; the comparison with eager execution is the only source of corrected-behavior evidence.

historical_conditions.statement: A CPU model compiled with torch.compile executes forward logic that applies torch.sum(x[self.idx], dim=1), where self.idx is a CPU tensor containing out-of-bounds indices ([[1, 3, 2], [1, 4, 3]]) for an input x with first dimension size 2.

defect_mechanism.description: The torch.compile-generated C++ path for indirect indexing x[idx] does not validate that idx is within bounds before accessing memory. Because the real index values are only known when the generated C++ code runs, an out-of-bounds CPU index results in an illegal memory read rather than the eager IndexError. The comment-thread diagnostic indicates that validation would need to be performed in the generated C++ code, in contrast to the Triton backend's device_asserts.

observed_failure.description: The torch.compile-compiled CPU model returned a tensor with nan and an anomalous large value (-1.7412e+38) in positions using out-of-bounds indices, while the same model without torch.compile raised IndexError: index 3 is out of bounds for dimension 0 with size 2.

historical_observations.statement: The issue body labels the compiled output as 'success, out-of-bound read' and shows nan and -1.7412e+38 in the output tensor.
Running the same input through func(input_tensor) without torch.compile raises 'IndexError: index 3 is out of bounds for dimension 0 with size 2'.
